post_text:
I sat across from him, my red pen hovering over his printed proposal like a surgeon’s scalpel.

He had spent three weeks building a vision for the new project, and I dismantled it in three minutes. I didn't raise my voice, but I didn't leave him any room to breathe either. I corrected every minor detail, imposing my preferences as if they were universal laws. I thought I was protecting the quality of our work, but I was actually suffocating the person who was supposed to run with it.

The silence that followed was heavy. He stopped arguing and just started nodding, his eyes losing the spark they had when he walked in. That was the moment I realized I hadn't won a debate; I had lost a partner. By demanding perfection according to my map, I had ensured he would never learn to navigate on his own. I traded his growth for my comfort. Now, I let people make mistakes that won't sink the ship, because a slightly imperfect plan owned by the creator is worth ten perfect plans forced upon a stranger. 🚢
lesson_extracted: True leadership requires sacrificing your own preference for perfection to allow others the space to find their own path.
